answer.reasoning: Operating margin is a standard, useful metric for a diversified industrial and manufacturing company like 3M, and 3M explicitly tracks 'Operating income margin' in its Results of Operations [5, 7]. In FY2022, 3M's consolidated operating income margin decreased by 1.7 percentage points, from 20.8% in FY2021 ($7,369 million operating income / $35,355 million net sales) to 19.1% in FY2022 ($6,539 million operating income / $34,229 million net sales) [5, 6]. By income statement component (as a percentage of net sales), this 1.7 percentage point decrease was driven by: (1) SG&A expenses increasing by 6.1 percentage points (from 20.4% to 26.5%) due to special item litigation costs (notably a ~$1.2 billion Q2 2022 pre-tax charge related to Combat Arms Earplugs litigation), impairment costs related to exiting PFAS manufacturing, costs related to exiting Russia, divestiture-related restructuring charges, and growth investments, partially offset by restructuring benefits and cost management [5]; (2) Cost of sales increasing by 3.0 percentage points (from 53.2% to 56.2%) due to special item litigation costs for PFAS-related commitments at the Zwijndrecht, Belgium site, inflationary pressures on raw materials and logistics, manufacturing productivity headwinds (supply chain issues, Belgium operations shutdown), and investments in growth/productivity/sustainability, partially offset by higher selling prices [2, 5]; and (3) Goodwill impairment expense increasing by 0.8 percentage points (from 0.0% to 0.8%, or $271 million) related to exiting PFAS manufacturing [4, 5, 6]. These negative drivers were partially offset by: (4) Gain on business divestitures improving operating margin by 8.0 percentage points (from 0.0% to -8.0% of net sales, or $2,724 million pre-tax gain) from the split-off and combination of the Food Safety business with Neogen Corporation [5, 6]; and (5) R&D expenses decreasing by 0.2 percentage points (from 5.6% to 5.4%) [5]. Additionally, 3M notes that remaining organic growth/productivity and other items yielded a net 1.3 percentage point benefit (despite a 0.3 percentage point headwind from lower disposable respirator demand), while foreign currency impacts (net of hedging) decreased operating income by ~$271 million [2].
answer.answer:
Operating margin is a useful and standard performance metric for a manufacturing company like 3M. In FY2022, 3M's operating income margin decreased by 1.7 percentage points, from 20.8% in FY2021 to 19.1% in FY2022. This change was driven by:

1. Higher SG&A Expenses (+6.1 percentage points of net sales, from 20.4% to 26.5%): Driven by special item litigation costs (primarily a ~$1.2 billion pre-tax charge for Combat Arms Earplugs litigation), PFAS manufacturing exit impairment costs, Russia exit costs, divestiture-related restructuring charges, and investments in growth initiatives, partially offset by restructuring benefits and ongoing cost management.
2. Higher Cost of Sales (+3.0 percentage points of net sales, from 53.2% to 56.2%): Driven by special item litigation costs for PFAS-related commitments in Zwijndrecht, Belgium, raw material and logistics inflation, manufacturing productivity headwinds (including global supply chain challenges and the shutdown of certain operations in Belgium), and investments in growth, productivity, and sustainability, partially offset by selling price increases.
3. Goodwill Impairment Expense (+0.8 percentage points of net sales, from 0.0% to 0.8%): Resulting from a $271 million goodwill impairment charge in the Advanced Materials reporting unit due to exiting PFAS manufacturing.
4. Gain on Business Divestitures (-8.0 percentage points of net sales, favorable impact): A $2.7 billion ($2,724 million) pre-tax gain from the split-off and combination of the Food Safety business with Neogen Corporation.
5. Lower R&D Expenses (-0.2 percentage points of net sales, favorable impact, from 5.6% to 5.4%).

Other cross-cutting drivers included a net +1.3 percentage point benefit from remaining organic growth/productivity and other items (which included strong pricing and spending discipline, partially offset by a -0.3 percentage point impact from lower disposable respirator demand) and an unfavorable foreign exchange impact of approximately $271 million on operating income.
